components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Primary action trigger (e.g. Quick Log, Save Transaction).
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #161d26; color: #ffffff; padding: 8px 16px; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; border: 1px solid #161d26; border-radius: 4px; letter-spacing: 0.02em; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s, border-color 0.15s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #25303f; border-color: #25303f; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Secondary filter, cancel, or auxiliary action button.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: #ffffff; color: #161d26; padding: 8px 16px; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; border: 1px solid #d2d9e4; border-radius: 4px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s, border-color 0.15s; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: #f4f6f9; border-color: #cbd5e1; }

components.name: Ledger Panel
components.description: Standard drafting vellum panel for metrics, accounts, and ledgers.
components.css: .ds-card { background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #d2d9e4; border-radius: 6px; padding: 16px; } .ds-card-title { font-size: 13px; color: #64748b; font-weight: 500; margin-bottom: 4px; } .ds-card-val { font-size: 24px; color: #161d26; font-weight: 700; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: Compact categorical chip for income, expense, and transfer states.
components.css: .ds-badge-inflow { display: inline-block; background: #ecfdf5; color: #059669; border: 1px solid #a7f3d0; border-radius: 9999px; padding: 2px 8px; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

components.name: Dimension Caliper
components.description: Signature budget progress bar with 80% and 100% threshold notches.
components.css: .ds-caliper { position: relative; height: 8px; background: #e5eaf0; border-radius: 4px; overflow: visible; } .ds-caliper-bar { height: 100%; background: #059669; border-radius: 4px; } .ds-notch { position: absolute; top: -3px; width: 2px; height: 14px; background: #94a3b8; } .ds-notch-80 { left: 80%; background: #d97706; } .ds-notch-100 { left: 100%; background: #dc2626; }

narrative.overview: Hisab approaches personal finance not as an abstract SaaS game or casual spending feed, but as intentional structural architecture. Every taka earned, spent, transferred, or saved is treated with drafting-table precision, dimensional accountability, and mathematical permanence. The visual atmosphere evokes the clarity of an architect's working drawing: calm, structured, high-density, and disciplined.
keyCharacteristics: Structural precision: crisp tabular alignment, explicit border lines, and zero floating-point ambiguities.
Functional color discipline: restrained palette where color carries strict operational meaning.
High-efficiency density: compact layout designed for rapid daily logging and clear monthly scanning.
Caliper thresholds: progress bars accented with dimension notches for budget limits and savings targets.

rules.name: The Strict Semantic Color Rule
rules.body: Color is never applied purely for decoration. Every hue on screen must communicate direction (income vs. expense), state (safe vs. warning vs. over-budget), or system identity (transfer vs. cash flow).

rules.name: The Tabular Numerals Invariant
rules.body: Any numeral representing currency, account balance, percentage, or date must render with tabular figures. Fluid proportional figures are forbidden in financial readouts.

rules.name: The Surface-Tonal Depth Rule
rules.body: Depth is created through surface tone contrast (#f4f6f9 ground to #ffffff panels) and 1px drafting borders (#d2d9e4). Diffuse, blurry drop shadows are prohibited; subtle crisp offset shadows appear only on interactive popovers, dropdowns, and modals.

dos: Do align monetary figures to the right in all tables and ledgers, with currency signs and minor units aligned.
Do visually separate transfers from income and expenses with distinctive transfer linking badges.
Do display budget thresholds with physical caliper notches (tick marks at 80% and 100%).
Do provide clear empty states with one-click creation triggers when an account or month has no posted transactions.
donts: Don't use decorative gradients, neon glows, or arbitrary accent colors unrelated to transaction type or budget state.
Don't use floating-point numbers in formatting; preserve integer minor units through formatters.
Don't obscure table columns on desktop; maintain high-density scanability.
Don't allow celebratory or gamified animations; maintain a dignified, trustworthy tool demeanor.
